subject: science
intro: In a chemical reaction, atoms rearrange and form new substances by gaining, losing, or sharing outer electrons. The periodic table helps predict reactions: metals (which lose electrons) tend to react with nonmetals (which gain electrons) to form compounds. For example, a reactive metal and a reactive nonmetal combine readily. By looking at the outer electrons of the reactants, we can predict and explain what products will form.

items.prompt: A reactive metal that loses one electron reacts with a nonmetal that gains one electron. Predict what happens and explain.

steps: The metal tends to lose its outer electron, and the nonmetal tends to gain one.
The electron transfers from the metal to the nonmetal.
This forms a compound made of the two elements, so they combine into a new substance.
solution.answer: The metal gives its electron to the nonmetal, and they combine to form a new compound.

items.prompt: Why do metals tend to react with nonmetals?

steps: Metals tend to lose outer electrons and nonmetals tend to gain them.
These tendencies fit together: one gives electrons and the other takes them.
So metals react readily with nonmetals, transferring electrons to form compounds.
solution.answer: Because metals lose electrons and nonmetals gain them, so they transfer electrons and combine into compounds.

items.prompt: A noble gas (last column) has a full outer electron level. Predict how reactive it is and why.

steps: Reactivity depends on gaining, losing, or sharing outer electrons.
A noble gas already has a full outer level, so it has little tendency to gain, lose, or share electrons.
So a noble gas is very unreactive.
solution.answer: It is very unreactive, because its full outer electron level gives it little tendency to react.

items.prompt: In a chemical reaction, what do atoms do with their outer electrons?

steps: Reactions involve the outer electrons of atoms.
Atoms gain, lose, or share outer electrons to form new substances.
solution.answer: They gain, lose, or share them to form new substances.

items.prompt: Two very reactive elements, one that loses electrons easily and one that gains them easily, are mixed. Predict the reaction.

steps: One element readily loses electrons and the other readily gains them.
These strong opposite tendencies make them react quickly.
They combine readily to form a compound, so a vigorous reaction is predicted.
solution.answer: They react readily, with electrons transferring, to form a compound.

items.prompt: Construct an explanation for why sodium and chlorine react to form a compound.

steps: Sodium is a metal that easily loses one outer electron.
Chlorine is a nonmetal that easily gains one outer electron.
Sodium transfers its electron to chlorine, and the two combine to form the compound sodium chloride.
solution.answer: Sodium loses an electron that chlorine gains, so they combine to form the compound sodium chloride.
